title: The Siege of Constantinople (1453), according to George Sphrantzes
author: George Sphrantzes (English translation; translator not named on host page)
publication: Chronicon Minus, siege excerpt (ch. 35), hosted by De Re Militari (Society for Medieval Military History)
notes: Near-eyewitness Byzantine courtier. Written after the events. Gives 4773 Greeks plus about 200 foreigners (=4973), 200000 Ottoman men, 400 vessels and an 18-mile circuit; dates the siege start as 4 April 1453 and the sultan's occupation of the straits as 26 March 1452 (other sources: 6 April and 15 April). The Ottoman figures are round and rhetorical. A different wording (4983 Greeks and just under 2000 foreigners) circulates in popular works and matches the later Chronicon Maius tradition - see S42/S43.
